title: Measure theory and integration
stage: Graduate study and qualifying exams in mathematics
audience: a graduate student in the first years of a mathematics PhD preparing for qualifying exams, or a graduate preparing to apply for one
purpose: Learn the foundation of modern analysis: σ-algebras and measures, outer measure and the construction of Lebesgue measure, measurable functions, the Lebesgue integral, the monotone and dominated convergence theorems and Fatou's lemma, modes of convergence, product measures and the Fubini–Tonelli theorem, L^p spaces and their completeness, signed measures and the Radon–Nikodym theorem, and differentiation of integrals.
primary_reading: Measure, Integration & Real Analysis by Sheldon Axler (free, open access)

weeks.1: Σ-algebras, measures and why they are needed
weeks.2: Outer measure and the construction of Lebesgue measure
weeks.5: The monotone convergence theorem and Fatou's lemma
weeks.7: Modes of convergence: almost everywhere, in measure and in L^p
weeks.8: Product measures and the Fubini–Tonelli theorem
weeks.9: L^p spaces: the Hölder and Minkowski inequalities and completeness
weeks.11: Signed measures and the Radon–Nikodym theorem

blocks.deliverable: Prove that every countable set has Lebesgue measure zero and outline the construction of a non-measurable set.
Compute Lebesgue integrals of supplied functions from the definition.
Justify or refute the interchanges of limits in supplied examples.
Week 7 midterm; compute an iterated integral and justify the order of integration.
Prove the completeness of L^1 and outline the density of continuous functions.
Apply the Radon–Nikodym theorem to a supplied pair of measures.
Submit the project; take an unseen 180 minute final in week 14.

project: Qualifying-exam dossier in real analysis: write complete solutions to twenty exam-style problems on measure, integration and L^p spaces with every theorem cited, prove the dominated convergence theorem and the completeness of L^p from the definitions, and build a plain-Python demonstration of convergence failures (moving bumps and escaping mass) that shows numerically why each hypothesis is needed.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
